chunks: And from him, from al-Nakha'i, from Safwan, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who arrived on the Day of Tarwiyah performing Tamattu' (Hajj) and did not have a sacrificial animal (hady), so he fasted on the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of Arafah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must fast one other day after the Days of Tashriq.'

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the day of standing at Arafah
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Tamattu' pilgrim who fasts on Tarwiyah and Arafah but has no sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the deficiency in the sacrificial animal (hady) for a Mutamatti' pilgrim is compensated by fasting, specifically prescribed as one day after the Days of Tashriq to ensure the expiation is completed after the prohibition of fasting during those days. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of substituting financial or ritual obligations with acts of worship when the primary requirement is unfulfilled due to lack of means. The specific timing after Tashriq ensures the pilgrim does not violate the distinct sanctity and rulings associated with the Eid al-Adha period.
